answer: Each agent must lock a bond scaled to its claimed reputation before earning, released only after the bond seasons. A Sybil attacker minting a thousand clones posts a thousand bonds from independently aged funds: the protocol keeps a cipher of funding provenance per deposit, so wallets sharing one origin merge into a single entity. Cost is linear for attackers (N bonds plus slash risk) but near-constant for honest agents. Proof-of-work per claim lifts a vote's price as identities grow, so the cheap inlet narrows and a haven of aged stake keeps its yield as duplicate clusters collapse.
